_source: The ore-vein registry of the pack (GTRegistries.ORE_VEINS: GTM 7.5.3, GT-- (gtnn), GT Community Additions (gtca), Gregicality Rocketry (gcyr)), as dumped by the validator (tools/analysis) and read live by the smoke test.
_how_it_is_used: Only the smoke test reads this file (tools/test/overlay/kubejs/server_scripts/gg_test_hv_multis.js; run it alone with the command gg_test_vein_coverage). It walks the live vein registry and FAILs for every vein that can generate in a dimension of the server and has neither a sample item (grindless:vein_sample_<id without namespace and '_vein'>, the name the validator looks for) nor a gtceu:vein_drilling recipe that takes it, so a mod that adds veins is caught the day it is added. This file is the explicit list of the veins that are allowed to have neither. Nothing in the game reads it.

Veins that cannot generate anywhere in this server are exempt without being listed: the test works out live whether a dimension of the vein's filter is loaded AND its layer applies there. The 14 GT-- '*_tf' veins (apatite_tf ... sapphire_tf) use the 'tf' layer, which only applies in twilightforest:twilight_forest; this pack has no Twilight Forest, so they never generate (every ore of them also comes out of a vein that is covered, so nothing is lost). The day that dimension loads they FAIL until they have samples and recipes.
An entry must stay true: the test FAILs when an excluded vein is already covered (delete its entry) and notes entries whose vein no longer exists.

veins = exact registry ids. dimensions = a vein is excluded when EVERY dimension of its filter is in the list, so a vein that also generates in the Overworld, Nether or End can never hide here. until = the era that brings the vein into the drill tables.
When a tier takes one of these veins: add it to veins_overworld_extra.json / veins_nether.json / veins_end.json (or veins.json) and delete its entry here.

removeFromWorld = true: server_scripts/grindless/moon/worldgen.js also takes the vein out of GTM's registry, so new chunks do not generate it any more (the entry stays as the record of why; the test then only notes that the vein is gone).

veins.reason: End vein of scheelite, tungstate and lithium. Tungsten comes from Mars (docs/journey.md, DECISIONS.md 2026-10-24), so the vein left the End table in v0.4.1 with its drilling recipes; its sample stays registered for old saves (hidden in EMI, it crafts back into an empty vein probe, startup_scripts/grindless/hv/family_items.js) but no recipe takes it. Since v0.5.0 (the End is MV, without ilmenite or scheelite) it no longer generates in new End chunks either. Nothing up to HV needs the vein: lithium also comes from the salts vein (lepidolite, spodumene) and from clay.

End vein of naquadah and plutonium 239. Naquadah only comes from Venus (docs/eras/iv.md, decision 4): the vein moved there as grindless:naquadah_vein_venus (data/grindless/tables/veins_venus.json, with its sample and, from the pressurized vein drill, its drilling recipes), and since IV it no longer generates in new End chunks.

End vein of pitchblende and uraninite. It stays in the world, and no drill takes it: the uranium in-situ leach field (in_situ_leaching recipes, not vein_drilling) works it with its sample grindless:vein_sample_pitchblende_end (data/grindless/tables/veins_leach.json; docs/eras/iv.md, decisions taken with the raise, 2). So the coverage test, which counts only vein_drilling recipes, keeps finding it uncovered: this entry stays.

dimensions.reason: Space dimensions of Gregicality Rocketry. GCYR's own 12 veins (Earth materials) are removed from the worldgen since v0.5.0 (server_scripts/grindless/moon/worldgen.js). Since IV, Venus and Mercury have one vein of ours each (data/grindless/tables/veins_venus.json and veins_mercury.json, added by server_scripts/grindless/iv/foundation.js, with their samples). The drills that take them (the pressurized vein drill on Venus and the Mercury vein drill) bring their vein_drilling recipes; delete this entry when both have them, or the test flags it as a stale exclusion.
